## 721: All Common-Divisor Sets and Greatest Values

Positive-divisor reading:

1. D+(20)={1,2,4,5,10,20}; D+(30)={1,2,3,5,6,10,15,30}.
   Intersection {1,2,5,10}; greatest common divisor 10.
2. D+(36)={1,2,3,4,6,9,12,18,36};
   D+(24)={1,2,3,4,6,8,12,24}.
   Intersection {1,2,3,4,6,12}; greatest 12.
3. D+(15)={1,3,5,15}; D+(30) as above.
   Intersection {1,3,5,15}; greatest 15.
4. D+(18)={1,2,3,6,9,18}; D+(35)={1,5,7,35}.
   Intersection {1}; greatest 1.

If "divisor" ranges over all nonzero integers, each of these full intersections
must also contain the negative of each listed positive member. Greatest values
remain 10,12,15,1, but the sets differ. Zero divides none of these nonzero
integers. The selected standalone definition does not specify the divisor
sign domain. A view can expressly ask positive common divisors, but this does
not settle the unrestricted original full-set convention. Retain that affected
task gap; the four positive maxima are convention-independent.

## 723: All Products, Sums and Differences Before Reduction

1. (2*3)/(4*5)=6/20=3/10 (divide2).
   (2*3)/(7*2)=6/14=3/7 (cancel common factor2).
   (5*4)/(4*9)=20/36=5/9 (cancel4).
   (7*5)/(2*7)=35/14=5/2 (cancel7).
2. (4*5)/(3*6)=20/18=10/9 (divide2).
   (15*3)/(11*10)=45/110=9/22 (divide5).
   (14*9)/(15*7)=126/105=6/5 (divide21).
   (2*3)/(9*8)=6/72=1/12 (divide6).
3. (12*5+12*9)/(12*3)=12(5+9)/(12*3)=14/3.
   (8*8-8*7)/(8*5)=8(8-7)/(8*5)=1/5.
   A factor can be cancelled from a sum only if it factors the entire sum.
4. (14*5-14*2)/28=14(5-2)/(14*2)=3/2.
   (19*8+19*6)/(7+12)=19(8+6)/19=14.
   The denominator 7+12 is first 19; its addends cannot be cancelled
   separately with factors of numerator addends.

All original denominators are fixed positive values; all twelve results are
dimensionless. Retain four product tasks per group and two sum/difference
tasks per group, not just demonstration of one cancelled factor.
